Apply latest spec changes for createParserOptions

This aligns with:
- https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12583
- https://github.com/w3c/trusted-types/pull/606

Key changes:
- Remove default `= {}` from `SetHTMLUnsafeOptions.sanitizer` and
  `ParseHTMLUnsafeOptions.sanitizer` in IDL,
  and only populate `sanitizer`
  on the dictionary passed to `createParserOptions` when provided.
- Update `TrustedTypePolicy.createParserOptions` and
  `CreateParserOptionsCallback` to accept optional
  `SetHTMLUnsafeOptions` and variadic `any... args`, passing
  `"TrustedHTMLParserOptions"` and the
  sink name when invoked on the default policy.
- Require default policy `createParserOptions` vetting when author
  supplied parser options specify `runScripts: true` or a non-empty
  sanitizer, even
  when the input is already a `TrustedHTML`. (This is a breaking
  change! but still protected by the flag)
- Allow any `TrustedHTMLParserOptions` (even without a sanitizer) to
  satisfy Trusted Types enforcement for HTML fragment sinks, and use
  `TrustedTypesCheckForFragment` in `Document.parseHTMLUnsafe`.
- Bypass `createParserOptions` and ignore sanitization in XML
  documents,
  always requiring `TrustedHTML` for XML fragment sinks.

Exclude X11GlobalShortcutListenerOzone from ChromeOS builds

Global shortcut listener on X11 is only used by Linux desktop
chrome. Move it under is_linux in BUILD.gn and guard the override
in OzonePlatformX11 with !IS_CHROMEOS so that the ChromeOS build
falls back to GlobalAcceleratorListenerChromeOS, as on devices.

With that, linux-chromeos registers the glic global hotkey with
ash's accelerator controller, which FocusManager::ProcessAccelerator
falls through to, so AcceleratorPressedDoesNotLaunchGlicWhen
LauncherEnabled can no longer distinguish local from global
handling. Exclude that test on ChromeOS.

gpu: Remove --disable-zero-copy-dxgi-video

The switch duplicates the disable_dxgi_zero_copy_video driver bug
workaround: both are read by SupportsZeroCopy() and disable the same
path. They have overlapped since the feature was enabled by default in
2016.

The workaround covers both uses. gpu_driver_bug_list.json applies it on
known-bad drivers, and --disable_dxgi_zero_copy_video sets it by hand.
The switch also required a GpuPreferences field, a mojom field and its
StructTraits.

TextureSelector::Create() and
D3DVideoDecoderBackend::CreateTextureSelector() no longer read
GpuPreferences, so that parameter is removed from both.

GpuPreferences is built in the browser process from the command line and
sent to the sandboxed GPU process at startup, so this drops one bool
from a trusted-to-sandboxed message and adds nothing. The workaround
that replaces it never crosses IPC: the GPU process computes it in
ComputeGpuFeatureInfo() from the driver blocklist and its own command
line.

[autopip] Don't synchronously close autopips as they open

When a page enters auto picture-in-picture after a delay (still within
the activation window) and the opener tab has already been refocused and
unoccluded by the time picture-in-picture opens,
AutoPictureInPictureTabHelper::MediaPictureInPictureChanged(true)
immediately exits auto picture-in-picture.

For video picture-in-picture, this tore down the session and notified
the renderer via OnStopped() inside
VideoPictureInPictureWindowControllerImpl::Show() before
PictureInPictureServiceImpl::StartSession() had returned the
StartSession callback to the renderer, leaving the renderer stuck
thinking the video was still in picture-in-picture. Instead, post
MaybeExitAutoPictureInPicture() to run asynchronously so the
picture-in-picture session can finish opening before it is closed.

[iOS] Gate bookmarks action sheet New Window on multipleScenesAvailable

Check _browser->GetSceneState().multipleScenesAvailable instead of
base::ios::IsMultipleScenesSupported() when configuring the single
bookmark action sheet in BookmarksHomeViewController.

Observe SceneState in BookmarksHomeViewController and dismiss the action
sheet if multiple scenes availability changes.

Note that the UX with this fix isn't great; the action sheet disappears
after the device has closed/opened/rotated. It could be nicer, but this
is UI that I expect is very rarely used, and this is a corner case
(action sheet open on a foldable device when the device changes
mutiwindow availabiliy), so I think it's OK to ship in a slightly janky
state.

[DCSI] Clear thread-local SharedContextState before recreating lost context

Clear the thread-local SharedContextState pointer before resetting the
previous lost context in CompositorGpuThread::GetSharedContextState()
and GpuChannelManager::GetSharedContextState().

When a SharedContextState is marked lost directly without going through
CompositorGpuThread::LoseContext() or
GpuChannelManager::LoseAllContexts(), the previous instance remains
stored in shared_context_state_ and registered in thread-local storage.
Calling GetSharedContextState() to recreate the context previously reset
or reassigned shared_context_state_ before clearing thread-local
storage, triggering CHECK_NE(GetForCurrentThread(), this) in
~SharedContextState() when the last reference was dropped.

Add a unit test in GpuChannelManagerTest to verify recreating a lost
SharedContextState updates thread-local storage without crashing.

Revert "[Extensions] Re-register service workers after storage wipe"

This reverts commit 8600522db4446ded022edfed2a790ef4a4eb4653.

Reason for revert: Luci suspected this https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/bisection/compile-analysis/b/8668675847695969105

Failure Link:https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/android-desktop-x64-archive-rel/22359/overview
Original change's description:
> [Extensions] Re-register service workers after storage wipe
>
> When //content detects service worker storage corruption, it deletes all
> stored data and recreates the context without notifying observers of
> individual deleted registrations. Registration requests in flight during
> the wipe fail with kErrorAbort, which is not retried. As a result,
> ServiceWorkerTaskQueue either keeps treating the wiped workers as
> registered (so later starts fail with kErrorNotFound) or gives up on the
> aborted registration, leaving extension workers broken until the browser
> restarts.
>
> Add OnStorageWipedSync() to ServiceWorkerContextObserverSynchronous,
> which is only used by extensions, and call it once recovery completes.
> On notification, ServiceWorkerTaskQueue resets registration and worker
> state (including in-flight start requests and scheduled retries) and
> re-registers the service workers of all enabled extensions in that
> context. Queued tasks run once the new registration starts the worker.
>

[Direct Offers] Reduce vertical padding for offer suggestions

Three-line Wallet Direct Offer suggestions had too large a gap between
them. Promo code rows received the generic 16dp vertical padding from
AddSuggestionContentToView(). Wrapped titles looked correct only because
CreateWalletDirectOfferRowContentView() overrode the padding to 8dp when
the main text did not fit on one line.

This CL applies the reduced 8dp vertical padding to all non-payment
3-row suggestions, replacing the Autofill AI-only special case and
resolving its TODO, and removes the now-redundant single-line check and
override in CreateWalletDirectOfferRowContentView() so wrapped and
single-line offers are padded consistently. Merchant promo codes are
currently the only non-payment suggestions that render three rows on
desktop.

[platform_util] Check AreShellOperationsAllowed in Mac OpenExternal

Unlike ShowItemInFolder() in platform_util_mac.mm, OpenItem() in
platform_util.cc, and OpenExternal() on Linux and Windows
(https://crrev.com/c/8501540), the macOS implementation of
platform_util::OpenExternal() did not check
platform_util::internal::AreShellOperationsAllowed().

Check internal::AreShellOperationsAllowed() in
platform_util::OpenExternal() on macOS so tests that call
DisableShellOperationsForTesting() (such as
ExternalProtocolHandlerBrowserTest in https://crrev.com/c/8501540) do
not invoke NSWorkspace to launch external OS protocol handlers during
tests.

[Views] Move views/autofill tests to per-directory targets

Move the browser_tests, unit_tests and interactive_ui_tests sources in
chrome/browser/ui/views/autofill/ and its autofill_ai/,
one_time_tokens/ and popup/email_verifier/ subdirectories out of
chrome/test/BUILD.gn into new per-directory source_sets, and drop the
leaf deps that only they needed.

  autofill:                browser_tests (1), unit_tests (4),
                           interactive_ui_tests (1, Windows only)
  autofill_ai:             browser_tests (3), unit_tests (2)
  one_time_tokens:         browser_tests (1), unit_tests (1)
  popup/email_verifier:    unit_tests (1)

This is part of an effort to shrink chrome/test/BUILD.gn by moving test
sources into per-directory targets.

Test counts are unchanged (identical test lists before and after):
  browser_tests  Linux 38283, ChromeOS 48525
  unit_tests     Linux 33858, ChromeOS 49265
The interactive_ui_tests file only builds on Windows; gn desc confirms
it is still compiled into interactive_ui_tests there.

gn check passes on Linux (debug and release), ChromeOS, ChromeOS device
(betty), Windows (x64 and x86), Mac and Android. The new targets compile
on Windows and Mac.

ConfigurationPolicyHandlerList and set it from
AreCloudOnlyPoliciesAllowed() in BuildHandlerList() (enabled when

Testing).

AtMemory: Remove local entity priority from duplicate resolution.

Previously, `PreferFirstResult()` prioritized local Chrome entities (`is_local`) over synced Server Wallet entities. This behavior conflicted with Ambient Autofill, which prioritizes Server Wallet entities over local entities.

Update `PreferFirstResult()` to resolve duplicate search results in this order:
1. Select the result with more non-empty metadata fields.
2. Select the result from the Autofill source over remote sources.
3. Select the result with the higher confidence score.

[IWA] Enforce BUILD.gn target visibility, assert_no_deps, and DEPS

Tighten GN target visibility across Isolated Web Apps, Web Package Rust,
and Controlled Frame targets, forbid //chrome/* dependencies in
//components/webapps/isolated_web_apps, and block production
//chrome/browser/ui/views includes in
//chrome/browser/web_applications/isolated_web_apps.

This improves module boundary enforcement and repository navigability,
raising the core IWA AI-First Readiness Score (go/iwa-ai-readiness)
from 72.33 to 75.64 / 100.

b90e3e95e1e7d1188cd961c41154b7dd5faf227b [ diff ] 
[Omnibox] Trim test keyboard debounce to 0ms & drop legacy delay

In test builds, KEYBOARD_DEBOUNCE_DELAY_MS (10ms) causes
Instrumentation.waitForIdleSync() in OmniboxTestUtils to return before
mKeyboardTransitionRunnable executes, and places mKeyboardTransitionRunnable
behind ViewRootImpl's 0ms MSG_CHECK_FOCUS when transferring focus to
FocusThief in clearUrlBarFocus().

Trim KEYBOARD_DEBOUNCE_DELAY_MS to 0ms in test builds so
mKeyboardTransitionRunnable still debounces synchronous back-to-back calls
in the MessageQueue while executing before MSG_CHECK_FOCUS and before
waitForIdleSync() returns. Also remove the legacy mKeyboardHideTask delay
from the non-debounced arm of setKeyboardVisibility and drop the unused
shouldDelayHiding / delayHide parameter across Omnibox.

Add --open-in-background to open command-line URLs without taking focus

A command line handed to an already-running browser always activates the
window its tabs land in: the first URL gets NEW_FOREGROUND_TAB, and
OpenTabsInBrowser() ends in an unconditional BrowserWindow::Show(),
which for an already-visible window is a straight Widget::Activate().
Launchers that only need to hand a URL to the browser the user already
has open have no way to avoid interrupting them; --no-startup-window and
--silent-launch suppress the window but also drop the URL.

Add --open-in-background, which opens command-line URLs as background
tabs and shows the target window without activating it. A window created
to host the URLs is still shown and activated, and so is the first tab
added to an empty window, since NormalizeDisposition() promotes a
background tab back to the foreground when the tab strip is empty.

Test: browser_tests --gtest_filter=StartupBrowserCreatorTest.*
Test: interactive_ui_tests --gtest_filter=StartupBrowserCreatorActivationTest.*

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers for HistoryMenuBridge

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

android: linker: UMA histogram for percentage of RELRO shared

In crrev.com/c/8495566 we started allowing partial RELRO sharing. Add a
simple process-agnostic metric to tell how much we are not sharing.

The buckets are logarithmically distributed because regressions on small
percentages are interesting in details, while missing a large chunk of
RELRO is a sign of the mechanism not being useful at all - no need in
granularity in this case.

tab_sharing: Migrate TabSharingStatusMessageView labels to ui::ColorId

This CL simplifies `TabSharingStatusMessageView` by setting its label
colors once at construction. Previously, this view was required to
manually handle theme updates by overriding `OnThemeChanged()`.

Following crrev.com/c/6267139 and crrev.com/c/6266947, we can pass the
`ui::ColorId` directly to `views::Label::SetEnabledColor()` and
`views::Label::SetBackgroundColor()`. The labels now automatically
handle theme changes, eliminating the need for manual color management.

cc48e7c4a024e558ed591ed88049ce9bb18763ab [ diff ] 
[iOS][Actor] Post FailCurrentTool so it is never applied on the tool's stack

`FailCurrentTool` could run from inside the tool and delete it while it
was still on the stack. `ToolController::FailCurrentTool` now applies
the failure from a posted task, bound to a weak pointer so it is dropped
if the tool completes or is cancelled first.

The tool is still failed eagerly rather than when it completes: on iOS a
navigation cancelled by a policy decider may send no
`DidFinishNavigation`, so tools waiting on it, and the observation
delay, would otherwise only finish on their timeouts.

[Testing] Readability enhancements for test failures

Test failures are now printed out in a much more pleasing, easy to read
format that includes:
 - The description of the current step
 - The reason for failure
 - The element or element identifier involved
 - Any subsequence failures
 - Any additional context
 - The "stack trace"
 - The element dump

Additional improvements:

Redundant or confusing information is no longer printed; for example,
either the element or its ID is printed, but not both, since the element
will print its ID (this is also the first time that if a live element
exists it will be printed). The same is true for "call stack" vs. step
number (if there is a call stack, no overall step number is printed).

More newlines are added to make the information easier to parse.

Timeouts will no longer produce duplicate callstacks, or a fail
callstack followed by a crash callstack (unless the test code does e.g.
a null deref after the test is failed; crashing after a timeout was
surprisingly common).

Test failure now looks like this:

```
Interactive test failed on step: AnyOf()
Reason: kSequenceTimedOut
ElementIdentifier: kInteractiveTestPivotElementId
Subsequence failures:

Subsequence 1 failed on step: CheckFirstResult()
Reason: kFailedForTesting
Element TestElement(ElementIdentifier: kInteractiveTestPivotElementId [address:0x1c400020150], ElementContext 0x1)
Nested steps (outermost to innermost):
  #0: In test, step 2: AnyOf()
  #1: In AnyOf()
  #2: step 1: CheckFirstResult()

Subsequence 2 failed on step: WaitForShow()
Reason: kSequenceTimedOut
ElementIdentifier: ../../ui/base/interaction/interactive_test_unittest.cc::72::kTestId1
Nested steps (outermost to innermost):
  #0: In test, step 2: AnyOf()
  #1: In AnyOf()
  #2: step 1: WaitForShow()

No stack available; step number is 2 UI Elements
  ╰─[CURRENT CONTEXT] ElementContext 0x1
     ╰─Pivot element (part of test automation)
```

Android: Replace View / Activity mocks with real objects (simple-1)

Mocking framework classes like View and Activity is discouraged, and
is disallowed by an Error Prone check. This replaces such mocks
in tests with real instances (e.g. new View(), new FrameLayout(),
Robolectric.buildActivity()) and removes the associated
@SuppressWarnings("DoNotMock").

[iOS] Use UIWindowSceneActivationAction for Open in New Window menus

Use UIWindowSceneActivationAction in BrowserActionFactory's
-actionToOpenInNewWindowWithURL:activityOrigin: and
-actionToOpenInNewWindowWithActivity: methods so UIKit can dynamically
show or hide the Open in New Window menu item based on whether scene
activation is currently allowed. This can vary by device posture and
orientation on the Duo, and this is the API recommended by Apple to
handle that scenario. This UIAction subclass handles the new scene
creation; instead of an arbitrary action block, it accepts a block that
returns the scene activation configs.

Given that, we now have two code paths for new window creation: the
existing scene command, and through UIWindowSceneActivationAction.
Accordingly, this CL also extracts
CreateWindowSceneActivationConfiguration() to window_activity_helpers so
BrowserActionFactory and SceneCoordinator share the same activation
configuration setup. That helper also attaches the menu scenario to the
NSUserActivity userInfo passed into the scene activation request. When
the new window connects, SceneController's
-recordWindowCreationForSceneState: records the OpenInNewWindow menu
action histogram.

HistoryUITestCase/testContextMenuOpenInNewWindow is also updated to
verify that a second foreground window opens rather than asserting
command dispatch.

0be084c96c99688d7e47bc68389fd9830a5ca4c1 [ diff ] 
Restore minimized browser window on tab activation

When a ChromeTabbedActivity window is minimized in Android desktop
windowing mode and tab activation is triggered (e.g., clicking "Back
to tab" in a Document Picture-in-Picture window),
ActivityTabWebContentsDelegateAndroid.bringActivityToForeground() only
called ApiCompatibilityUtils.moveTaskToFront(). While moveTaskToFront()
reorders visible or occluded tasks, it does not unminimize a minimized
window on Android Desktop.

Update bringActivityToForeground() to look up the target activity's
window ID via TabWindowManagerSingleton and launch the bring-to-front
intent via MultiWindowUtils.launchIntentInInstance(), matching the
existing ChromeLauncherActivity.bringTabActivityToFront() pattern.
Because launchIntentInInstance() invokes AppTask.startActivity() on the
matching task, Android Desktop Windowing properly unminimizes and
restores the browser window. Fall back to moveTaskToFront() if the
window ID is INVALID_WINDOW_ID (e.g., for non-tabbed activities).

[PageInfo] Record sliced UMA metrics for PageInfo surface

Adds support for slicing PageInfo metrics based on the entry-point
surface (e.g. standard omnibox PageInfo vs Contextual Tasks side
panel Super G button).

Specifically:
- Adds Surface enum to PageInfo and plumbs it through
  PageInfoBubbleSpecification.
- Slices WebsiteSettings.Action,
  WebsiteSettings.OriginInfo.PermissionChanged, and
  WebsiteSettings.OriginInfo.PermissionChanged.{Allowed,Blocked} by
  PageInfoSurface token variant (ContextualTasks).
- Refactors surface-specific histogram logging in PageInfo with

[BottomBar] Animate both offsets on browser-driven controls show

Since crrev.com/c/7868827, runBrowserDrivenShowAnimation() off the NTP
takes its start offset and animator range from the top controls only.
With the controls scrolled off, a tab-modal JS dialog
(ChromeTabModalPresenter calls showAndroidControls(true)) animates the
top offset but writes a bottom offset of 0 on every frame. The bottom
controls pop fully in for a few frames (~75ms on an emulator) before the
renderer's offsets take over and slide them in again. With the address
bar at the bottom, the top offset is already 0, so the show returns
early and leaves offsetOverridden set with no animator. The renderer's
next offset update clears it, so that case isn't visible.

The hide path likewise sets offsetOverridden before checking whether
there is anything to animate, and times the animation from the top
controls only.

* Show: animate both offsets to 0, timed by the larger hidden ratio.
  Return without setting offsetOverridden (and reset a latch left by a
  cancelled hide) when both offsets are already 0.
* Hide: only set offsetOverridden once an animation starts, and time it
  by the remaining travel of the controls that move.

Verified on an emulator (top address bar, controls scrolled off, JS
alert): without this change the bottom bar pops in and then slides in
again; with it both bars slide in once. Regression tests in
BrowserControlsManagerUnitTest fail without the fix.

[BottomBar] Do not re-show dismissed update badge on profile switch

`UpdateMenuItemHelper.onMenuButtonClicked()` only updates
`UpdateStatusProvider` for `UNSUPPORTED_OS_VERSION` and is a no-op for
`UPDATE_AVAILABLE`, leaving `getUiState().buttonState` non-null.
Previously, `BottomBarAppMenuUpdateBadgeController` unconditionally
re-bound `mUpdateMenuItemHelper` on every profile supplier notification
(even when `profile.getOriginalProfile()` resolved to the same helper
instance) and computed badge visibility solely from `uiState.buttonState
!= null`, causing a dismissed update badge to reappear when switching
between regular and incognito modes.

* Short-circuit `mProfileObserver` when the resolved
  `UpdateMenuItemHelper` instance is unchanged across regular and
  incognito profile switches.
* Track badge dismissal via `mIsBadgeDismissed` so `updateBadgeState()`
  suppresses the badge until `mMenuStateObserver` notifies of a state
  update, `uiState.buttonState` becomes null, or the helper instance
  changes.
* Call `dismissUpdateBadge()` before `onMenuButtonClicked()` on menu
  visibility changes to match `ToolbarManager`.

[SendTabToSelf] Filter out invalid TimeSentToReceived samples

This CL stops recording TimeSentToReceived during MergeFullSyncData or
when an entry was already opened before Sync finished downloading it,
and renames the histogram to Sharing.SendTabToSelf.TimeSentToReceived2
since filtering out these samples changes the distribution.

Initial sync downloads historical entries when a device signs in, which
should not be counted as live delivery latency. Additionally, on iOS,
push notifications allow opening a shared tab before Sync downloads the
entry, which previously caused TimeSentToReceived to exceed
TimeSentToOpened.

OBSOLETE_HISTOGRAM[Sharing.SendTabToSelf.TimeSentToReceived]=Replaced by
Sharing.SendTabToSelf.TimeSentToReceived2

parent
db4c6c5af1ec364b7f3234e26d029c18ec90c357 [ diff ] 
[base] Add AlignedCalloc() and use it for Dawn wire buffers

To get zeroed aligned memory, code calls AlignedAlloc() or
AlignedUninit() and then fills the memory with zeros. For a large
allocation, this writes to every page, so every page gets physical
memory. When PartitionAlloc is malloc, it direct-maps allocations
larger than its largest bucket (983040 bytes), so their pages are new
pages from the OS, which are zeroed already.

Add base::AlignedCalloc(num_items, size, alignment), which returns
zeroed aligned memory that is freed with AlignedFree(). Add
base::AlignedZeroed<T>(capacity, alignment), which returns it as an
AlignedHeapArray<T>, like AlignedUninit<T>(). AlignedZeroed() only
accepts arithmetic types and std::byte, whose value is zero when all
their bytes are zero.

When PartitionAlloc is malloc, AlignedCalloc() uses
allocator_shim::UncheckedAlignedCalloc() (crrev.com/c/8479893) for the
sizes that PartitionAlloc always direct-maps. PartitionAlloc doesn't
zero their pages again, and the pages that are never written are never
faulted in. On Apple platforms, this is only done after PartitionAlloc
replaces the default malloc zone, because free() can't free the shim's
memory before that. If UncheckedAlignedCalloc() returns null,
AlignedCalloc() calls TerminateBecauseOutOfMemory(), so that the crash
is reported as out of memory, like when AlignedAlloc() fails.

For smaller sizes, and in other builds, AlignedCalloc() uses
AlignedAlloc() and memset(). These allocations usually reuse freed
memory, which has to be zeroed anyway, and calloc() would zero their
whole slot rather than only the requested size. Both ways return zeroed
memory, so the size check only affects performance.

Each WebGPU decoder in the GPU process owns a DawnServiceSerializer,
which has two 1 MiB buffers that were filled with zeros. Use
AlignedZeroed() for them. In a local run of a WebGPU page on macOS, 1
of the 64 pages (16 KiB each) of each buffer was resident, instead of
all 64: 32 KiB instead of 2 MiB per decoder.

Time to allocate and free with an alignment of 64 when the memory isn't
used (Apple M4 Pro, release build, fastest of 2 runs):

  Size          AlignedAlloc() + memset()  AlignedCalloc()  Speedup
  983041 bytes  42.6 us                    5.8 us           7x
  1 MiB         45.4 us                    6.5 us           7x
  4 MiB         171 us                     10.9 us          16x
  16 MiB        674 us                     26.3 us          26x
  64 MiB        2.79 ms                    27.7 us          100x

When every page is used, it's 7-12% faster. Sizes up to 983040 bytes
run the same code as before.

Tests:
* AlignedMemoryTest.AlignedCalloc: the memory is aligned and zeroed for
  sizes on both sides of the threshold, after freeing memory with
  non-zero bytes that the allocator can reuse.
* AlignedMemoryTest.AlignedCallocMultipleItems and
  AlignedMemoryTest.AlignedZeroed.
* AlignedMemoryDeathTest.AlignedCallocOverflow: num_items * size
  overflows.
* OutOfMemoryDeathTest.AlignedCalloc and SecurityAlignedCalloc: too
  large sizes crash, as with AlignedAlloc().

[FedCM] Add tests for account sort order ties

AssembleAndSortAccounts() uses std::stable_sort with a comparator that
treats two accounts as equal when both are filtered out, both are newly
logged in, or both are non-returning (kSignUp). In these cases the order
returned by the IdP is preserved.

No existing test covered these equal cases, so a change to the
comparator could silently reorder the accounts shown to users. This CL
adds tests that pin the current behavior.

This issue was spotted during the review in
crrev.com/c/8499923/comment/70d507cf_0d0ccc2c/

[ash] auto_screen_brightness: take the profile path in ModellerImpl

ModellerImpl reads and writes the personal model under the profile
directory, and held a Profile solely to call GetPath() on it. It takes
the path directly instead, which is also what its own
GetModelSavingSpecFromProfilePath() already operates on, so the class no
longer references Profile at all and its header drops
chrome/browser/profiles/profile.h. An empty path disables the modeller,
like a null Profile did.

Controller resolves the path where it builds the modeller. The unit test
drops its TestingProfile, which existed only to supply a path under the
fixture's temp dir, so chrome/test/base is now test-only in this
directory's DEPS.

#ai-assisted

efc532cb187180d5fbc6d11f23df0b43f73fdfb6 [ diff ] 
[Android] Redirect native test stdout with dup2() instead of freopen()

freopen() on stdout closes fd 1 before dup'ing the new file onto it.
In browser tests, other threads are already running when
JNI_NativeTest_RunTests() redirects stdout, and if one of them opens a
file in that window it gets fd 1 (and may wrap it in a unique_fd).
freopen() then dup3()s over it and fdsan aborts when stdio takes
ownership of fd 1:

  fdsan: failed to exchange ownership of file descriptor: fd 1 is owned
  by unique_fd ..., was expected to be unowned

This shows up as rare EXECUTION_ERRORED results in android_browsertests
where the test process crashes before the test starts.

Open the stdout file and dup2() it onto STDOUT_FILENO instead, which
replaces fd 1 atomically so it is never free.

TAG=agy
CONV=4e98b4a0-1b61-4298-882b-92a10e60c5d6

Use ForegroundServiceUtils for GracefulShutdownService

Move maybeStartGracefulShutdown() from GracefulShutdownService (in
base_module_java) to GracefulShutdownServiceImpl (in chrome_java), and
update it to use ForegroundServiceUtils to launch the service instead of
calling Context.startForegroundService() directly.

Previously, integration tests that mocked ForegroundServiceUtils (such
as TabAlertIndicatorTest) would still start the real
GracefulShutdownService during activity teardown in
ChromeActivity.onDestroy(), but onStartCommand() would hit the mocked
ForegroundServiceUtils.startForeground() no-op, crashing the test
process with RemoteServiceException.

[IAU 3/4] Implement InAppUpdateController engine and unit tests

Chrome on Android is introducing support for Google Play In-App Updates
using non-blocking flexible updates to reduce the mobile patch gap
caused by background auto-update gating. Update downloads occur
in the background while browsing and stage on disk for a restart
snackbar.

This CL implements the InAppUpdateController engine and unit tests:

- Uses Play Core's AppUpdateManager to detect update availability, start
  flexible background downloads, observe download progress via
  InstallStateUpdatedListener, and complete installation by relaunching
  Chrome.
- Triggers discovery and restart prompts via
  InAppUpdateSnackbarController, and integrates with InAppUpdatePolicy
  for build eligibility and independent throttling (discovery decline,
  restart decline, and download failure).
- Telemetry: Adds the InAppUpdateDownloadResult enum (FLOW_STARTED,
  SUCCEEDED, and terminal failure buckets) and the corresponding
  Android.InAppUpdate.Download.Result histogram.
- Unit Tests: Implements unit tests in InAppUpdateControllerTest
  using FakeAppUpdateManager, exercising core user journeys, state
  machine transitions, and Activity lifecycle edge cases.

This is part 3a of the in-app update series.

Activity lifecycle wiring and app menu integration are deferred to
https://crrev.com/c/8412767/

Additional test updates from sorin@'s feedback in:
https://crrev.com/c/8522677

51592c22a9e2409a9aa9b7e6acd10d523cdf8cba [ diff ] 
Keep preselected auto-added tab state

When the user confirms a tab picker selection (such as adding a second
tab) without touching a preselected auto-added tab,
`attachSelectedTabsWithWebStateIDs:` previously cleared `isAutoAdded` on
all items in `selectedWebStateIDs`. That promoted the untouched
auto-added tab to a user attachment as a side effect of selecting
another tab.

Stop clearing `isAutoAdded` on preselected items in
`attachSelectedTabsWithWebStateIDs:`. Deselecting the tab and confirming
with the checkmark button removes the auto-added item, so reopening the
tab picker, reselecting the tab, and confirming again still attaches it
as a user attachment.

[Blink] Simplify AcceleratedSBI::CreateFromRaster()

Removes the redundant recorder.HasReleasableDrawOps() conditional in
AcceleratedStaticBitmapImage::CreateFromRaster() (mirroring
UnacceleratedSBI::CreateFromRaster() [1]):
- All callers of CreateFromRaster() unconditionally emit draw operations
  in draw_callback [2][3][4].
- Even if a caller produced an empty PaintRecord, RasterSharedImage(...,
  /*needs_clear=*/true) must still be invoked on the newly created
  ClientSharedImage so that BeginRasterCHROMIUM(...,
  /*needs_clear=*/true) [5] clears the backing to background_color and
  marks it as cleared on the GPU service.

[TabRestoreService] Return stored entry SessionID from create APIs

Make TabRestoreService::CreateHistoricalGroup and BrowserClosing return
std::optional<SessionID>, and tighten CreateHistoricalTab so that all
three creation methods return the SessionID of the top-level entry
actually stored in TabRestoreServiceHelper::entries_ (or std::nullopt if
the entry was filtered out or not created).

Previously, CreateHistoricalTab returned local_tab->id even when
AddEntry() dropped the entry via FilterEntry() (e.g., an unpinned NTP),
and CreateHistoricalGroup / BrowserClosing returned void. Returning the
stored entry's SessionID allows Android's HistoricalTabSaver to key
tab-closure undo off the TabRestoreService entry in follow-up CLs.

[Blink] Inline SharedImagePool::GetImage() in CreateFromRaster()

Inlines SharedImagePool::GetImage() [1] and
SharedImagePoolBase::CreateSharedImageInternal() [2] into
AcceleratedStaticBitmapImage::CreateFromRaster() to directly create the
ClientSharedImage, eliminating the single-use SharedImagePool and
CanvasResourceSharedImage in CreateFromRaster().

Note that:
- GetImageFromPoolInternal() always returns nullptr because image_pool
  was just created and is empty.
- image_info.is_software is false and image_info.buffer_usage is
  std::nullopt.
- SharedImagePool::Create() [3] and
  ClientSharedImageInterface::CreateSharedImage() [4] never return
  nullptr in production, so the null checks on image_pool and resource
  are dropped.
- Eliminating SharedImagePool and CanvasResourceSharedImage is a no-op
  with respect to their constructors and destructors:
  - The constructors of SharedImagePoolBase [5],
    CanvasResourceSharedImage [6], CanvasResource [7], and ClientImage
    [8] only initialize member fields.
  - ~SharedImagePoolBase() [9] is a no-op because no images are released
    into the pool, and ~CanvasResourceSharedImage() [10] and
    ~ClientImage() [11] are no-ops because client_ is nullptr and
    subclass_manages_destruction_sync_token_ is true.

[OE][2/2] Exclude hidden windows from macOS native screenshare picker

When triggering screenshare from OmniboxEverywhere on macOS,
SCContentSharingPicker runs out-of-process in replayd and can still
hit-test the hidden OmniboxEverywhere NSWindow's bounds if WindowServer
has not yet flushed its order-out or if an asynchronous AutoResize
updates the hidden window's frame. This caused the 'Share Window' button
to occasionally flicker when hovering over the area where the widget was
located.

This change:
1. Populates SCContentSharingPickerConfiguration.excludedWindowIDs in
   NativeScreenCapturePickerMac::Open with all hidden Chrome NSWindows
   sothey are excluded from the native picker.
2. Defers ResizeDueToAutoResize while the screenshare picker is open so
   the hidden NSWindow does not trigger setFrame:display:YES while the
   picker is active.

Demo: https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NjYyMTk0MDEyNjA1NjQ0OHxlN2E5MGE4Yi0zYw

Cache macOS character font fallback

Extend CharacterFallbackKey on macOS with optional exact codepoint and
fallback priority fields so non-ideographic fallback characters (such as
Hiragana, Katakana, CJK punctuation, and UI symbols) are cached per
character in character_fallback_cache_ rather than re-invoking CoreText
cascade and Skia typeface creation on every HarfBuzzShaper::ShapeSegment
call. Ideographic characters continue to share a single cache entry
verified via unicharToGlyph().

Also:
- Cache the last 4 CTFontRef -> identifier keys in BuildIdentifierKey()
  with precomputed string hashes.
- Guard IsAppleColorEmojiFont() with Character::IsEmoji(character) and
  defer CTFontCopyCharacterSet() in GetAlternateFontPlatformData() until
  traits or weight differ.

[Android] Do not freeze PDF NativePage on reparenting in TabImpl

Freezing a `PdfPage` during tab detachment (`updateAttachment(null,
null)`) or hidden reattachment (`updateAttachment(window,
tabDelegateFactory)`) calls `PdfPage#destroy()` ->
`PdfCoordinator#destroy()`, removing `ChromePdfViewerFragment` from
`FragmentManager` and discarding unsaved PDF annotations.

* Exempt unfrozen PDF pages (`!mNativePage.isPdf()`) from
  `detachAndFreezeNativePage()` when detaching from an `Activity` in
  `TabImpl#updateAttachment()`.
* Route unfrozen PDF pages through `maybeShowNativePage()` on
  reattachment even when hidden so they rebind to the new `Activity`,
  while keeping already-frozen PDF pages frozen.

Revert "[Minimal UI] Remove special case for CCT toolbar in minimal UI"

This reverts commit 93855053ab2ae968c4422cf2188cea5849033b64.

Reason for revert: Breaks use-case that partners rely on

Failure Link: b:432128207, https://crbug.com/564533651

This patch has a few extra changes to make sure that the behavior works
correctly:
1. Guard against desktop devices and fullscreen mode in
   `TrustedWebActivityBrowserControlsVisibilityManager` and
   `BaseCustomTabActivity`: `AppHeaderUtils.checkIsInDesktopWindow()`
   relies on `captionBarInset.top > 0`. When a desktop window enters OS
   or HTML5 fullscreen, the caption bar hides and `mIsInDesktopWindow`
   becomes `false`. To avoid regressing Bug 419636269 by showing the
   mobile CCT toolbar in fullscreen, `computeBrowserControlsState()` now
   also requires `!DeviceInfo.isDesktop()` and
   `!mFullscreenManager.getPersistentFullscreenMode()`.
2. Add unit tests in
   `TrustedWebActivityBrowserControlsVisibilityManagerTest` verifying
   that browser controls remain hidden when exiting desktop windowing
   due to fullscreen mode or on desktop devices.
3. Update `org.chromium.chrome.test.R` to `org.chromium.chrome.R` in
   `WebappDisplayModeTest` to resolve resource import changes since the
   original commit.

Original change's description:
> [Minimal UI] Remove special case for CCT toolbar in minimal UI
>
> Previously, we would show the CCT toolbar if the page was using
> `minimal-ui` display mode even if the URL was in the manifest's scope.
> The toolbar was not shown in this way for other display modes such as
> `standalone`.
>
> This CL removes the CCT banner special case for `minimal-ui` in
> non-desktop windowing mode. The CCT banner special case was already
> disabled for desktop windowing mode.
>
> Bug: 419636269

WebUI Toolbar: Fix MemorySaverChipInteractiveTest

Fix several test failures in MemorySaverChipInteractiveTest when
WebUILocationBar, WebUIBatterySaverButton, and
WebUIPerformanceInterventionButton features are enabled. This is a
test-only change.

Root causes and fixes:

1. WebUI shadow DOM click targeting: In WebUI location bar mode, the
clickable button resides inside the <page-action-chip> shadow DOM.
PressPageActionButton() previously used
PressButton(kMemorySaverChipElementId), which dispatched clicks directly
to the custom element host without triggering the inner button click
handler (notably when the chip was in icon mode).

Fix: Updated PressPageActionButton() in the test fixture to use
InvokePageAction(kActionShowMemorySaverChip, InputType::kKeyboard),
which delegates via PageActionTestAccessor::Click() to traverse the
shadow DOM.

2. Reopen suppression of synthetic clicks: WebUIBubbleReopenSuppressor
debounces pointer clicks that arrive within
kMinimumTimeBetweenButtonClicks of the bubble closing, to absorb
asynchronous WebUI click events that would otherwise reopen a bubble the
user just dismissed. Several tests (e.g.
ModifyExceptionsListOnCancelButtonClick) dismiss the bubble and
immediately press the chip again, faster than any real user could, so a
pointer-triggered reopen was swallowed. The fixture previously worked
around this with SetSuppressionThreshold(0), but disabling the debounce
re-exposes the real race for MousePressPageActionButton()'s genuine
mouse clicks and made CancelButtonStatePreservedWhenSwitchingTabs flaky.

Fix: PressPageActionButton() now opens the bubble with a keyboard
trigger instead of a pointer click. Keyboard triggers are never
debounced by WebUIBubbleReopenSuppressor, so the tests can reopen the
bubble immediately without lowering the threshold, and the
SetSuppressionThreshold(0) override is removed. Mouse clicks (via
MousePressPageActionButton()) keep the production debounce.

Note: WebUIBubbleReopenSuppressor is slated to be replaced by WebUI-side
logic. Whatever replaces it must continue to exempt keyboard-triggered
opens from debouncing, or these tests will break.

3. Tab switch synchronization: In
CancelButtonStatePreservedWhenSwitchingTabs and
ChipCollapseRemainCollapse, switching tabs previously interacted with
the new tab's page actions without waiting for web contents visibility
or navigation reload completion.

Fix: Added WaitForShow(contents_id) and content::WaitForLoadStop() after
SelectTab() steps.

download: Fix crash for deep scanned opened dangerous item

In DownloadItemNotification::GetSubStatusString(), the check for
`item_->IsInsecure() || item_->IsDangerous()` runs before the check for
`DOWNLOAD_DANGER_TYPE_DEEP_SCANNED_OPENED_DANGEROUS`. Because
`DownloadItemImpl::IsDangerous()` returns true when the danger type is
`DOWNLOAD_DANGER_TYPE_DEEP_SCANNED_OPENED_DANGEROUS`,
`GetSubStatusString()` delegates to `GetWarningStatusString()`, where
`case download::DOWNLOAD_DANGER_TYPE_DEEP_SCANNED_OPENED_DANGEROUS:`
previously broke out of the switch and hit `NOTREACHED()`.

Move the `IDS_PROMPT_DOWNLOAD_DEEP_SCANNED_OPENED_DANGEROUS` handling
into `GetWarningStatusString()` and remove the unreachable branch in
`GetSubStatusString()`. Add a unit test covering a download item with
`DOWNLOAD_DANGER_TYPE_DEEP_SCANNED_OPENED_DANGEROUS` and `IsDangerous()
== true`.

Bug: None
Test: unit_tests --gtest_filter=DownloadItemNotificationTest.DeepScannedOpenedDangerous

TabFootprintAggregator maintained three separate std::map<PageId, ...>
members, two std::map<base::ProcessId, ...> members, and a temporary

SpellCheckCustomDictionary: Keep words while spell checking is disabled

addWords() and removeWords() did nothing while spell checking was
disabled. If the user later turned spell checking back on, words the
page had added were flagged again.

Always forwards the words to the client, which keeps the document's word
set regardless of the enabled state.

[ash] auto_screen_brightness: take the PrefService in Adapter

Adapter consults two screen-brightness policy prefs to decide whether
the model may change brightness, and held a Profile solely to reach
them. It takes the PrefService by reference instead and keeps it as a
raw_ref, so the class no longer references Profile at all.

Controller resolves it where it builds the adapter, and the unit test
does the same from its TestingProfile. The prefs are now always present,
so the null check around the policy lookup goes away.

#ai-assisted

Further reduce binary size in TextInputManager

Follow-up to https://crrev.com/c/8502050 that reduces
text_input_manager.o .text by an additional 3,590 bytes (-8.3% in
optimize_for_size builds):

- Replace the 3 heap-allocated std::vectors and 2 std::sort calls in
  SelectionBoundsChanged() with a 4-corner min/max loop when computing
  the transformed bounding box.
- Delete copy/move operations on ViewState instead of defining unused
  out-of-line move operations (ViewState is constructed in-place via
  try_emplace).
- Avoid copying keys into a temporary std::vector in
  ~TextInputManager() before unregistering remaining views.
- Fold Windows proximate_character_bounds_map_ into ViewState and
  avoid duplicate map lookup in GetTextSelection().

[Extensions] Re-register service workers after storage wipe

When //content detects service worker storage corruption, it deletes all
stored data and recreates the context without notifying observers of
individual deleted registrations. Registration requests in flight during
the wipe fail with kErrorAbort, which is not retried. As a result,
ServiceWorkerTaskQueue either keeps treating the wiped workers as
registered (so later starts fail with kErrorNotFound) or gives up on the
aborted registration, leaving extension workers broken until the browser
restarts.

Add OnStorageWipedSync() to ServiceWorkerContextObserverSynchronous,
which is only used by extensions, and call it once recovery completes.
On notification, ServiceWorkerTaskQueue resets registration and worker
state (including in-flight start requests and scheduled retries) and
re-registers the service workers of all enabled extensions in that
context. Queued tasks run once the new registration starts the worker.

[webauthn] Record hybrid QR engagement in the modal

Add WebAuthentication.Hybrid.QrEngagement, recorded once per attempt
in which the WebAuthn modal dialog showed the hybrid QR code. It
reports whether a scan was detected (i.e. a BLE advert was received
from the phone), and covers all WebAuthn requests, including those on
the Chrome sign-in page.

The delegate now observes step transitions to detect when the modal
reaches the QR code step. Signin.HybridPasskey.InlineQrEngagement is
unchanged, but its enum moves to the webauthn enums as
WebAuthenticationHybridPasskeyEngagement so both histograms share it.

The existing engagement tests are parameterized to cover both the
inline Autofill QR code and the modal QR code.

[webauthn] Record hybrid outcome for all requests

Signin.HybridPasskey.Outcome only measures hybrid passkey success rates
for requests made on the Chrome sign-in page. Add
WebAuthentication.Hybrid.Outcome, which records the same outcome for
every WebAuthn hybrid request, including those on the Chrome sign-in
page. Secure Payment Confirmation requests are excluded.

The hybrid stage tracking and outcome recording code is no longer
gated on ENABLE_DICE_SUPPORT, so the new histogram is also recorded on
non-DICE platforms. The sign-in histograms are still only recorded for
Chrome sign-in requests, which can only happen on DICE builds.

The outcome enum is shared by both histograms and is moved from
signin/enums.xml to webauthn/enums.xml as
WebAuthenticationHybridPasskeyOutcome.

The existing hybrid outcome unit tests are parameterized to run both
for a regular website and for the Chrome sign-in page.

[SearchPrefetch] Consolidate prefetch request and expiry timer maps

SearchPrefetchService maintained parallel std::map<GURL, ...>
containers for active SearchPrefetchRequests and their expiry timers,
and performed redundant map lookups via operator[] and DeletePrefetch()
after find().

Consolidate the request and expiry timer into a single PrefetchEntry
struct in prefetches_, add ErasePrefetch(PrefetchMap::iterator) to
erase directly from existing iterators, and reuse find() iterators
across prefetches_ and prefetch_cache_. This reduces
search_prefetch_service.o .text by 2,526 bytes (-8.19%).

cb8028e6d1253d51ddd33a88e715c5f7906e14c5 [ diff ] 
convert_dict: drop morphological descriptions and accept tabs in rules

An SFX/PFX rule may end with a morphological description after its
condition, as in

  SFX A 0 ed . is:past / participle

Hunspell only uses it for morphological analysis, which Chromium never
requests, but AffReader::AddAffix scanned the whole line. It took the
first '/' anywhere as the start of the continuation flags and any '-'
as an old Hungarian morph rule, so a slash or a dash in a description
produced bogus aliases.

AffReader also only recognized spaces between fields, while Hunspell
accepts tabs too. Rules separated by tabs kept their continuation flags
as text, which Hunspell then reads as the wrong alias index.

Turn tabs into spaces as each line is read, and drop everything after
the condition of a rule before parsing it. This also removes the
rewrite of old Hungarian morph rules.

Rules and words may also refer by number to descriptions stored once in
a table of AM lines. Nothing refers to that table once the numbers are
dropped, so drop the AM lines too.

This fixes the Galician dictionary, which has rules with a slash or a
dash in their description. With gl-1-0.bdic every inflected Galician
word is flagged.

4f080e321119f1c7d3acd040ac61eb02b88fb66d [ diff ] 
[iOS] Use ColumnTime() and BindTime() in DownloadRecordDatabase

sql::Statement has ColumnTime() and BindTime() for base::Time columns
and asks callers to use them instead of converting through int64
microseconds by hand. DownloadRecordDatabase still converts by hand
when it binds the paging cursor, writes created_time and
completed_time, and reads them back.

Use BindTime() and ColumnTime() instead. The on-disk format is
unchanged: both accessors use the same microseconds since the Windows
epoch as the hand-written conversions. A null completed_time is still
stored as 0, because BindTime() writes 0 for a null base::Time and
ColumnTime() reads 0 back as a null base::Time. The old read also
dropped negative values, but this class never writes them, so every
row it stores reads back the same.

R=sdefresne@chromium.org

[signin] Make device_id_helper its own component

Move device_id_helper.{h,cc} from static_library("base") into
component("device_id_helper"), and the three functions they declare are
annotated with COMPONENT_EXPORT(SIGNIN_DEVICE_ID_HELPER). ":base" keeps
the target in its public_deps, so its dependents are unaffected.

This lets code outside the static library link against these functions
in a component build. The follow-up moves the existing ChromeOS-only
GenerateSigninScopedDeviceId(bool) here out of //chrome/browser/signin,
and its process-lifetime cache has to have a single definition for every
caller in a session to observe the same ID.

[ios][deflake] Fix synchronization flakes in BookmarksFolderChooserAccountTestCase

Improve test-only synchronization in BookmarkEarlGreyUI and
BookmarksFolderChooserEGTest to resolve flaky timeouts and element
interaction failures in BookmarksFolderChooserAccountTestCase,
BookmarksFolderChooserLocalTestCase, and
BookmarksFolderChooserSignedOutTestCase.

Specifically:
- Replace immediate assertWithMatcher visibility and non-visibility
  checks with waitForSufficientlyVisibleElementWithMatcher and
  waitForUIElementToDisappearWithMatcher on folder picker and editor
  views during creation, renaming, and moving flows.
- Synchronize context bar Done button tap and wait for edit mode to
  exit and context bar to return to default state before navigating
  into child folders.
- Ensure undo snackbar and keyboard dismissals complete before

[ash] Scope more test-only //chrome DEPS allowances to their tests

Twenty-five more directories where a +chrome allowance is only ever used
by tests. Each such entry moves from include_rules into
specific_include_rules, keyed on the test files that actually need it,
so production code in these directories can no longer pick the
dependency up by accident.

Only directories that had no specific_include_rules block are
touched, so no existing key changes meaning.

Whole-tree checkdeps passes. As a control, adding one of the scoped
includes to a production file now fails with "Illegal include ...
Because of -chrome".

#ai-assisted

[omnibox] Add bubble window-switch test and one-shot check helpers

* Adds WindowSwitchWhileBubbleActiveDismissesPopup. It switches windows
while a bubble is active, so neither the browser nor the popup widget
gets an activation change and only the paint-as-active subscription can
blur the omnibox.
* Adds one-shot versions of the polling focus and popup-state helpers, to make focus validation tighter.
* Make tests start on NTPs, so we have more test coverage. Currently, these tests start with `about:blank`. Starting with the NTP is the default case for a browser where a user didn't change their startup page. And this gives us more coverage for the "Views Omnibox to WebUI Omnibox handoff" story.

Fix timeouts in rVFC before-xr-session WPT

`request-video-frame-callback-before-xr-session.https.html` shares one
5s video between its 4 subtests, and starts playing it while the page is
still loading. On slow bots, the video can end before the subtests are
done. rVFC callbacks then stop, and the test times out. This happens on
~4% of win-rel runs.

This CL loops the video, and removes the Linux `[ Pass Timeout ]`
expectation, which should no longer be needed. It also removes a
`video.currentTime = 0` call, which never reset the video between
subtests.

[Direct Offers] Only use the Wallet Direct Offer row for promo codes

In `CreatePopupRowView()`, `kMerchantPromoCodeEntry` was the last label
of a long case list, so every suggestion type above it (addresses,
credit cards, footers, ...) fell into its block. With
`kAutofillEnableWalletDirectOffers` enabled, all of them were rendered
with `CreateWalletDirectOfferRowContentView()`, i.e. with a multi-line
main text capped at two lines.

Give `kMerchantPromoCodeEntry` its own case so that only promo code
suggestions get the Wallet Direct Offer row.

Also remove the flag check from that case. The other promo code
suggestion types are deprecated, so Wallet Direct Offers are the only
ones left, and their suggestions are only generated while
`kAutofillEnableWalletDirectOffers` is enabled.

[Blink] Inline CanvasResourceSI::Initialize() in CreateFromRaster()

Inlines CanvasResourceSharedImage::Initialize() [1] and its
WaitSyncToken() call [2] into
AcceleratedStaticBitmapImage::CreateFromRaster(). Because resource is
only used to obtain GetSharedImage() and acquire_sync_token() before
being destroyed at the end of CreateFromRaster(), and neither
~CanvasResourceSharedImage() [3] nor ~ClientImage() [4] reads any of the
fields set by Initialize() (client_ is nullptr and
subclass_manages_destruction_sync_token_ is set to true in the
CanvasResource constructor [5]), the only effect of Initialize() is
setting acquire_sync_token_ to shared_image->creation_sync_token() and
calling shared_image->UpdateDestructionSyncToken() if that token has
data.

Note that setting sync_token to shared_image->creation_sync_token()
unconditionally is equivalent to WaitSyncToken() only setting
acquire_sync_token_ when HasData() is true (because a SyncToken with
!HasData() is identical to acquire_sync_token_'s default-constructed
SyncToken()).

[1]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_resource.cc;l=181-200
[2]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_resource.cc;l=375-382
[3]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_resource.cc;l=263-275
[4]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:gpu/command_buffer/client/shared_image_pool.cc;l=35-40
[5]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_resource.cc;l=70-77

[MaliciousApkDownloadCheck] Dismiss dialog when DownloadItem is removed

Previously, DangerousDownloadDialogBridge did not notify Java when
native destroyed or completed/cancelled the underlying DownloadItem,
leaving open or queued dialogs in DangerousDownloadDialogBridge and
ModalDialogManager that retained the Android Activity and WindowAndroid.

This CL resolves this by:
1. Adding DangerousDownloadDialog#dismiss() to clear the result callback
   and dismiss the dialog with DISMISSED_BY_NATIVE.
2. Tracking active DangerousDownloadDialog instances by GUID in
   DangerousDownloadDialogBridge and adding dismissDialog() to remove
   pending queued dialogs, dismiss active dialogs, and clean up the
   activity state listener when OnDownloadDestroyed() (or
   OnDownloadUpdated() for done downloads) fires.

Composebox: Add Large Content Viewer to Plus menu attachment cards

In the Composebox Plus menu (`ComposeboxMenuViewController`), the
attachment cards cap their title font at 24pt (`kTitleMaxPointSize`) and
keep a fixed-size icon to fit in the horizontal grid. At accessibility
text sizes, users had no way to enlarge the card icon and full title.

mid-word at large accessibility sizes or clip in verbose languages;
crbug.com/570402750 will follow up once UX decides on a scrollable row
or vertical list layout.

and resets its `UILargeContentViewer` properties and interaction.

[PM] LoadingPageVoter V2: don't boost unsolicited background loads

LoadingPageVoter boosts every loading page in a background tab to
kUserVisible, including loads nobody asked for, such as timer-driven
location.reload() or meta-refresh.

This CL adds PageNode::IsUserOrBrowserInitiatedLoad(), set by
PerformanceManagerTabHelper when a primary main frame navigation starts,
so that the new renderer gets the right priority before commit. A
navigation qualifies if it is browser-initiated or has transient user
activation. A renderer-initiated navigation without activation that
starts within 10 seconds of the previous commit is treated as a client
redirect (e.g. link shorteners, SSO) and inherits that document's value,
based on content::RedirectChainDetector's heuristic. The window restarts
on each hop, so a page that reloads itself more often than every 10
seconds keeps the value of the load that opened it.

With the new PMLoadingPageVoterV2 feature, background loads are boosted
only when this property is true. V2 also keeps voting while the page is
kLoadingTimedOut, in any tab. Active tab loads are unchanged
(kUserBlocking).

PMLoadingPageVoter (V1) keeps its current behavior, for diagnostics
only. It takes precedence over V2 and will be removed when V2 launches.

Also adds process_priority_browsertest.cc, which checks the process
priority during whole page loads in common user scenarios.

[SigninPrefs] Add SigninPrefsAccessor [4/9]

Add `SigninPrefsAccessor` (in the `:signin_prefs_internal` GN target) to
provide a privileged generic accessor for the per-account signin
preference dictionary (`"signin.accounts_metadata_dict"`):

- Access is restricted via `base::PassKey<SigninPrefs, SigninPrefsAccessor>`
  and GN `visibility`.
- Every per-account key-based read, write, and clear is `CHECK`-validated
  against `SigninPrefsRegistry` (and `CHECK`s that `gaia_id` is non-empty).
- Corrupted non-dict intermediate entries (or account entries) are
  ignored on read (returning defaults without mutating prefs) and
  overwritten on write via `EnsureDict`; `MigrateObsoleteAccountPrefs`
  drops non-dict account entries alongside obsolete keys.
- `ClearPref` inspects `GetUserPrefValue` before opening a
  `ScopedDictPrefUpdate` so no-op clears do not fire spurious pref
  change notifications.
- Add direct unit tests for `SigninPrefsAccessor` operations, corrupted
  pref handling, and `CHECK` failure death tests.

The next CL [5/9] delegates `SigninPrefs` to `SigninPrefsAccessor`.

[ash] arc: take the NssService by constructor in CertManagerImpl

CertManagerImpl takes the NssService it imports into by pointer and
holds it as a raw_ref, so the class no longer references Profile at all,
and ArcServiceLauncher resolves the service where it builds the manager.

chrome/browser/ash/arc/net was the only production user of
chrome/browser/profiles in that directory, so the allowance is dropped
from DEPS and BUILD.gn. chrome/browser/net stays, the NssService type is
declared there.

CertManagerImplTest installs a FakeNssService, whose ChromeOS
constructor looks the user up for the profile, so it needs a logged-in
user session. It gets one from UserSessionTestEnvironment with
ChromeUserSessionTestEnvironmentDelegate and takes the browser context
from BrowserContextHelper, so the test does not mention Profile either.
Its crypto::ScopedTestNSSDBs are created before the fixture's own so
that they tear down in reverse order. Both //chrome dependencies it
needs are scoped to it in specific_include_rules.

This does not make the lookup meaningfully earlier. ArcServiceLauncher
already builds CertStoreService, whose factory DependsOn
NssServiceFactory, a few statements later in the same function.

#ai-assisted

This reverts commit ae2a7c2c07521aad903e4594721620b790899904.

Reason for revert: consistently fails android-desktop-x64-rel.

ContextMenuManagerUnitTest#testShouldShowItem_MultiWindow and LaunchInte
ntDispatcherTest#testDispatchGlicExternalTrigger_WithConversationId_Rout
esToTabbedActivity has failed in 3/25 recent builds of android-
desktop-x64-rel, every attempt in every one of them. This is not flake:
it reproduces on every run, so it blocks the CQ for every unrelated CL
that touches this suite. The regression appears at
refs/heads/main@{#1712049}.

Example failing run:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/try/android-desktop-x64-rel/787460

Replacing the SharedPreferencesManager fallback in
ChromeMultiInstancePersistentStore.readAllInstanceIds() with `assert
sData != null` (line 43) causes a deterministic java.lang.AssertionError
at ChromeMultiInstancePersistentStore.java:43 ->
MultiWindowUtils.getPersistedInstanceIds(MultiWindowUtils.java:1313) in
ContextMenuManagerUnitTest#testShouldShowItem_MultiWindow and LaunchInte
ntDispatcherTest#testDispatchGlicExternalTrigger_WithConversationId_Rout
esToTabbedActivity because those Robolectric unit tests do not call
MultiWindowTestUtils.resetInstanceInfo() to initialize sData before
invoking MultiWindowUtils.

Reverting to green the tree first. Please re-land once the failure is
understood and covered; this revert is about restoring CQ throughput,
not about the merit of the change.

[SigninPrefs] Add SigninPrefsRegistry [3/9]

Add `SigninPrefsRegistry` (in the `:signin_prefs_internal` GN target) to
maintain the canonical compile-time descriptor table of all registered
per-account signin preference keys, their `base::Value::Type`s, parent
dict paths, and whether string prefs store serialized `base::Time`
timestamps:

- `SigninPrefsRegistry::GetAll()`, `Find()`, and `IsValidValue()` are
  gated behind `base::PassKey<SigninPrefsRegistry>` (and a test-only
  `CreatePassKeyForTesting()` helper).
- `static_assert`s in `signin_prefs_registry.cc` enforce at compile time
  that `kRegisteredPrefs` is strictly sorted by `(parent_keys, key)` for
  `std::ranges::binary_search`, that every entry is well-formed, that
  non-empty `parent_keys` point to a registered `DICT` container, and
  that `kRegisteredPrefs` and `kDeprecatedTopLevelPrefs` are disjoint.
- Add unit tests covering registry lookup and `IsValidValue` type and
  timestamp validation.

Follow-up CLs add `SigninPrefsAccessor` [4/9] and delegate `SigninPrefs`
to it [5/9].

Android: Replace View / Activity mocks with real objects (medium-3)

Mocking framework classes like View and Activity is discouraged, and
is disallowed by an Error Prone check. This replaces such mocks
in tests with real instances (e.g. new View(), new FrameLayout(),
Robolectric.buildActivity()) and removes the associated
@SuppressWarnings("DoNotMock").

[Glic] Add GlicReuseCookies feature to reuse cookies during cookie sync

Adds a `kGlicReuseCookies` feature flag (disabled by default) and
exposes it via `chrome://flags/#glic-reuse-cookies`.

When enabled, `GlicCookieSynchronizer::BeginCookieSync()` uses
`gaia::MultiloginMode::MULTILOGIN_PRESERVE_COOKIE_ACCOUNTS_ORDER`
instead of `MULTILOGIN_UPDATE_COOKIE_ACCOUNTS_ORDER`, setting
`reuseCookies=1` on OAuthMultilogin requests so existing cookies can be
reused if possible.

[FedCM] Consolidate per-IDP maps and optimize account sorting for binary size

- In webid::Metrics, consolidate 5 parallel std::map<GURL, ...> members
  (provider_to_fedcm_idp_builder_, provider_source_ids_,
  accounts_request_sent_, accounts_dialog_shown_, and
  mismatch_dialog_shown_) into a single std::map<GURL, ProviderInfo>
  with out-of-line special members and a SumOverProviders() helper.
- In webid::Request and IdentityProviderInfo, move per-IDP accounts and
  filtered_accounts vectors into IdentityProviderInfo (eliminating two
  parallel base::flat_map<GURL, ...> maps), initialize
  IdentityProviderInfo's copy constructor via member initializer list,
  sort accounts with a stateless comparator after computing
  display_priority, and avoid redundant idp_infos_ map lookups in
  OnIdpMismatch(), ShowErrorDialog(), and MaybeShowNativeAppUi().

Measured .text reduction in out/Size:
- obj/content/browser/browser/metrics.o: 18,460 B -> 16,281 B (-2,179 B, -11.80%)
- obj/content/browser/browser/request.o: 121,514 B -> 118,200 B (-3,314 B, -2.73%)
- obj/content/browser/browser/identity_provider_info.o: 7,838 B -> 6,312 B (-1,526 B, -19.47%)
- Total across the 3 objects: -7,019 B (-4.75%)

[textdecoder] Reset CJK state after flushing

ISO-2022-JP and EUC-JP retain decoder state after end-of-input, allowing
one TextDecoder session to affect the next.

Reset ISO-2022-JP state after EOF processing and clear EUC-JP's JIS0212
selection using the existing Finalize hook. Preserve state while
streaming.

Keep the codec reuse optimization introduced in CL 2271061 to avoid
allocating a new codec for each decoding session.

clicked.
